function: PPO agent jointly sets the base station's ISAC transmit beamforming and movable antenna positions to maximize worst-case secrecy rate under a radar SINR constraint (pp. 3-4).
system: BS with 4 transmit movable antennas and 1 fixed receive antenna, 3 users, 1 eavesdropper, 1 radar target; 2.4 GHz; no RIS (pp. 1, 4).
method: Deep reinforcement learning: on-policy PPO actor-critic with generalized advantage estimation and clipped loss, trained by interaction with the simulated environment (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom simulator: far-field field-response channel with 13 paths, Gaussian path gains, path-loss exponent 2.2; bounded eavesdropper CSI error; no dataset or measurement (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: One simulated setting with uniformly random user positions; sweeps over power, sensing SINR threshold, antenna and path numbers; no train-test shift stated (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: A2C, TD3, DDPG; each also run with fixed-position antennas (FPA); no non-learned method compared (p. 4).
metrics: Worst-case secrecy rate (b/s/Hz), reward versus episodes for convergence; radar sensing SINR only as a constraint (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "we consider the far-field channel model from the CUs to the"; custom field-response channel with Gaussian path gains, and no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "as a function of the number of antenna elements"; the paper never says a trained model is tested on an unseen setting, and each sweep point appears to need its own training.
q3_support: p. 4: "Actor Critic (A2C), TD3 and DDPG"; all baselines are learned, also in FPA form, and no non-learned method such as random, fixed or optimization-based design is compared.
q4_support: p. 3: "This results in high computation cost" is said of one-shot optimization; the paper reports no complexity order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime for PPO.
q5_support: p. 4: "model parameters are listed in Table I"; channels are simulated, no code or data link is given, and no public dataset is used.
notes: Area 5: beamforming in an ISAC system, although the objective is secrecy rate; secrecy beamforming is not an excluded function. A movable antenna is not a RIS, so ris=0. The FPA curves are the same learned algorithms without antenna movement, so they are variants, not non-learned baselines. Table I read from the page image of p. 4. The text names DDQN once on p. 4, apparently meaning DDPG.
